key_findings: R reaches 1.025432 m/s at recorded 32.305 s, with its desired reference slew still within 100 rad/s². That reference bound does not bound actual acceleration or LQR torque.

At 32.250 s both solver and estimated support change belt B to shell B. The shell-B request is −7.718970 N m, clipped to −0.60 N m; the LQR jump is dominated by the −7.601677 N m gain-change term, with −0.011469 N m error-change contribution.

The platform already has large balance and rotational errors before this handoff. Its moderate current estimated rolling condition, 3.734659, differs from the earlier +0.9 rad near-singularity episode.
The instantaneous guarded-reference contribution softens shell-B demand by +0.097545 N m at the same frozen state and gain. It does not identify or remove preceding policy-history effects.
N has lower peak speed and 50 ms acceleration RMS in this fixed context, but short transients remain and no I52 candidate passes the complete cross-phase policy screen.
causal_limits: A command sampled at an endpoint acts over the next hold, not the velocity increment ending at that endpoint.
Solver contact truth is the last 1 ms endpoint sample, not a full 5 ms hold mean.
The command origin is identified algebraically; the unique physical cause of the whole coupled burst is not established by one saved history.
